question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to replace the italicised word in the given sentence.

I am astonished to see her *mercurial* demeanour in making any task a success.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Invariable**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"mercurial"** means someone who is subject to sudden or unpredictable changes of mood or mind. (अस्थिर)

 
 
• **Example:** Her mercurial nature makes it difficult to predict how she will react to any situation.
 
 
 
• **"Invariable"** refers to something that is unchanging and constant. (अपरिवर्तनीय)
 
 
• **Example:** His invariable commitment to his work earned him great respect among his peers.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'mercurial'** is **'invariable'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Invariable**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Fluctuant** (अस्थिर): Something that changes frequently and unpredictably.

 
 
• **Example:** The stock market is quite fluctuant these days.
 
 
 
• **Capricious** (मनमौजी): Given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behavior.
 
 
• **Example:** The capricious weather has made it hard to plan outdoor events.
 
 
 
• **Erratic** (अनिश्चित): Not even or regular in pattern or movement; unpredictable.
 
 
• **Example:** His erratic driving behavior caused concern among other drivers.
